edges.label: Deputy Secretary of Defense
edges.note: The Senate voted 59-40 on 14 March 2025 to confirm Stephen A. Feinberg as Deputy Secretary of Defense, the department's number-two official and the office that has historically signed the memoranda standing up DoD UAP bodies. No sourced UAP, AARO or PURSUE role for Feinberg personally was found.

edges.label: Principal Deputy Director, then Acting Director, NRO
edges.note: NRO's official leadership page lists Adkins as 'Acting Director, NRO' and states he 'was appointed Principal Deputy Director, National Reconnaissance Office (PDDNRO), on 12 January 2026,' with 'overall day-to-day management of the NRO.'

edges.label: CIA officer detailed to NRO advanced systems
edges.note: Per his NRO bio: 'From 1997 to 2000, Mr. Adkins worked for the Central Intelligence Agency and was assigned to the NRO in the Advanced Systems and Technology Directorate, where he managed several technology development projects.'

edges.label: House Appropriations Defense subcommittee staff overseeing NRO/NSA/NGA
edges.note: Before becoming PDDNRO he 'served on the professional staff of the House Appropriations Committee, Subcommittee on Defense, where he led the subcommittee's oversight and legislative responsibility for the NRO, U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, National Security Agency, and U.S. Cyber Command' - the panel that writes the classified defense appropriations annex.

edges.label: Staff Director, House Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee
edges.note: From 2000 to 2006 Adkins served on the House Science Committee and was appointed Staff Director for the House Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee, leading legislative and oversight activity over NASA and other civilian space agencies.

edges.label: questioned witnesses at the 26 July 2023 UAP hearing
edges.note: Chairman Grothman recognised Biggs, who questioned Grusch, Graves and Fravor about 'misdirection by official U.S. Government with regard to UAPs,' the 1997 Phoenix Lights, training-range impacts and over-classification.

edges.label: pressed Grusch on Phoenix Lights and withheld information
edges.note: Biggs asked Grusch about the 1997 Phoenix Lights case ('Only what is in the public vernacular about it. That was outside the scope of my duties') and asked whether DoD or intelligence agencies are 'keeping this information from the American people or even from Congress.'

edges.label: elicited Grusch's authorship of the UAPTF 2019 classification guide
edges.note: Asked by Biggs whether the 2019 UAP classification guidelines impede transparency, Grusch answered: 'I am familiar with the UAP Task Force 2019 Security Classification guide. I think it is fair. I did actually help author that with the Director.' Biggs replied, 'Uh-oh. You got a bias then.'

edges.label: questioned witnesses at the 26 July 2023 UAP hearing
edges.note: Frost used his round to question Ryan Graves and David Fravor on NASA's independent study team, stigma reduction and how Congress can 'facilitate partnerships between the scientific community and the UAP focus groups within government.'

edges.label: questioned Graves on scientific advisory board and NASA reporting
edges.note: Frost asked Graves how NASA research might influence commercial aviation safety and about 'the importance of seeking scientists to sit on your advisory board'; Graves pointed to NASA's Aviation Safety Reporting System as a near-term reporting platform.

edges.label: questioned Administrator Nelson on UAP; pressed NASA's role at hearing
edges.note: Frost told the hearing he sits on the Science, Space and Technology Committee and that when questioning NASA Administrator Bill Nelson about full funding, one of the reasons given 'had to do with UAPs.' He framed his questions around NASA's UAP independent study team.

edges.label: author of Sol Science and Policy Briefing No. 3
edges.note: Von Rennenkampff is the named author of 'First Peer-Reviewed Scientific Analysis of Possible UAP Materials Employs State-of-the-Art Technologies,' The Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings No. 3, April 2026.

edges.label: delivers the monthly Sol Briefing; authors Sol policy briefings
edges.note: His Sol Foundation author note states: 'He delivers the Sol Briefing, the Sol Foundation's monthly update on UAP news, and has been a regular contributor to The Hill.' He wrote Sol briefings No. 1 (January 2026) and No. 3 (April 2026).

edges.label: checked and rejected Kirkpatrick's balloon explanation
edges.note: After Kirkpatrick attributed tic-tac-shaped sightings to a Florida company's escaped helium balloons, von Rennenkampff wrote in The Hill: 'After calling the company, I found Kirkpatrick's statement to be implausible.' The Debrief quotes the op-ed and identifies him as a former State Department Bureau of International Security and Nonproliferation analyst.

edges.label: Obama-administration DoD appointee
edges.note: His Sol Foundation biography states he 'served as appointee in the US Department of Defense during the Obama administration and later worked in the US State Department.'

edges.label: co-host holding an unaired Grusch 'pre-interview'
edges.note: In the Need To Know episode 'David Grusch: He's Still Here' (24 June 2023), hosted by Zabel with Ross Coulthart, the episode note states: 'And Bryce adds: there's a second interview - actually the pre-interview - that Need to Know controls.'

edges.label: co-hosted 'Elizondo Unplugged' interview
edges.note: Elizondo appeared with Coulthart and Zabel on the Need To Know episode 'Elizondo Unplugged' (13 September 2024), discussing his book Imminent, crash retrievals and non-human intelligence.

edges.label: Sec. 1683 is the UAP-office provision of P.L. 117-81
edges.note: Section 1683 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81, 27 December 2021) is titled 'Establishment of office, organizational structure, and authorities to address unidentified aerial phenomena.'

edges.label: statutory basis for standing up AARO
edges.note: The Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum of 15 July 2022 approved amendments to the AOIMSG direction 'to meet the DoD requirements in section 1683 of the NDAA for FY 2022,' establishing the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office to carry out the duties assigned to AOIMSG.

edges.label: directed disestablishment of the UAPTF
edges.note: 'Consistent with section 1683 of the NDAA for FY 2022, I also direct the Secretary of the Navy to disestablish the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF) no later than the date the AARO is established, and to support the orderly transition of the UAPTF, including the transfer of any data, analysis, or other relevant material, to the AARO.'

edges.label: office required to be established in coordination with the DNI
edges.note: The FY2022 NDAA 'was enacted with a provision that requires the Secretary of Defense to establish an office, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence (DNI)'; the Deputy Secretary acted 'following coordination with the DNI' and copied the DNI on the AARO establishment memo.

edges.label: enacted as Division G of the FY2024 NDAA
edges.note: The Senate Select Committee on Intelligence publishes the enacted text as 'Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, Division G of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024' (P.L. 118-31, 22 December 2023).

edges.label: AARO reporting change and UAP funding limitation
edges.note: Division G contains Sec. 7341, 'Modification of reporting requirement for All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office,' and Sec. 7343, 'Funding limitations relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena' - the provision barring funds for UAP activity not disclosed to the AARO Director and congressional leadership.

edges.label: section node of this act (section number needs verification)
edges.note: The board's section node is filed under this act. Caution: the contractor turn-in language (persons holding UAP material or 'non-earth origin or exotic' material to notify AARO and make it available within 180 days) is Sec. 1104 of S.2103 as reported by SSCI on 22 June 2023; the enacted Division G UAP sections are numbered 7341 and 7343. The '1102' designation in the node id is not confirmed against either text.

edges.label: Reid is the principal behind the 2008-2009 DIA engagements
edges.note: AARO's Historical Record Report Volume 1 states: 'At the direction of Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid (D-NV), the Defense Appropriations Acts of Fiscal Years 2008 and 2010 appropriated $22 million for the DIA to assess long-term and over-the-horizon foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States.'

edges.label: $22M congressionally directed to DIA for advanced aerospace threat work
edges.note: Per AARO HRR Vol. 1: 'In coordination with the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, DIA established AAWSAP in 2009... The contract for this DIA-managed program was awarded to a private sector organization.' The report also notes DIA 'did not seek, nor specifically authorize' some of the resulting work.

edges.label: the engagements that produced AAWSAP
edges.note: AARO's official history places AAWSAP (2009-2012), also known as AATIP, directly downstream of Reid's direction and the resulting DIA appropriation.

edges.label: 24 June 2009 Reid SAP request refused by the Deputy Secretary
edges.note: 'On 24 June 2009, Senator Reid sent a letter to then Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that AAWSAP/AATIP be made a DoD Special Access Program. Deputy Secretary Lynn declined to do so based on the recommendation of then-Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, James R. Clapper, Jr., that such a designation was not justified.'

edges.label: publisher of Science and Policy Briefing No. 3
edges.note: The briefing is issued in The Sol Foundation Science and Policy Briefings series (No. 3, April 2026, published online 30 April 2026) and carries the foundation's imprint and cofounders Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish on the colophon.

edges.label: briefing analyses Nolan's Council Bluffs materials study
edges.note: The briefing's subject is the SIMS and MIBI analysis led by Stanford professor Garry P. Nolan with Jacques Vallee, Sizun Jiang and Larry Lemke of the 1977 Council Bluffs, Iowa molten-metal sample, published in Progress in Aerospace Sciences 128 (2022).

unresolved: steve-feinberg: no sourced UAP/AARO/PURSUE role found. His SASC advance policy questions (armed-services.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/feinberg_apqs_022525.pdf) and the 25 February 2025 SASC nomination transcript (armed-services.senate.gov/imo/media/doc/25-08_02-25-2025.pdf) contain no instance of 'UAP', 'AARO', 'anomalous' or 'unidentified'. The only edge offered is his institutional post. If a signed DepSecDef memo establishing or governing PURSUE surfaces, that would be the edge to add.

william-b-adkins: no UAP-specific document names him. He is wired on verified institutional grounds (NRO, CIA, House Appropriations Defense, NASA oversight). The premise that he is 'named in UAP legislative history' was not corroborated by any source found; Adkins Strategies' only visible lobbying registrations concern NASA authorisation and space launch.

iaa-fy2024-sec-1102: section number appears wrong. The enacted UAP sections in Division G of P.L. 118-31 are Sec. 7341 (AARO reporting) and Sec. 7343 (funding limitations relating to UAP). The contractor turn-in / 'non-earth origin or exotic UAP material' language is Sec. 1104 of S.2103 as reported by SSCI on 22 June 2023. Recommend renaming the node or verifying against the enacted text before relying on '1102'.

congress.gov could not be fetched; the 26 July 2023 hearing text was verified via the govinfo mirror CHRG-118hhrg53022. The Hill also blocks fetching, so von Rennenkampff's Hill columns are cited via URL plus The Debrief's verbatim quotation of the op-ed rather than direct page verification.

bryce-zabel: only two defensible edges found (Grusch and Elizondo, via Need To Know episodes). No sourced link to sol-foundation, ttsa, uapda-2023 or immaculate-constellation was located; reports that Grusch first told his story on camera at Zabel's home trace to secondary aggregators and were not used.

reid-dia-meetings-2008-2009: AARO's Historical Record Report describes the Reid-directed appropriation and the 24 June 2009 Lynn letter but does not name the contractor. A baass edge is therefore not asserted here; the BAASS award under solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 needs a primary DIA/FOIA document before wiring.
